subject: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benito Ruiz <benito@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request

Team —

Orion Health (Benito) is ready to start a 3-week production pilot for their low-latency triage workflow. They want predictable latency during business hours and have asked for a block of dedicated GPUs rather than relying solely on burst lanes. High level ask: a temporary reservation of 6-8 A100-class slots (single-GPU workers) Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 PST for 3 weeks, with autoscale disabled for that window (they want zero preemption during office hours).

Notes attached: pilot MAP (orion_pilot_map.pdf) and their traffic forecast (traffic_forecast.csv). Key constraints from the customer:
- 95th percentile < 120ms token latency for their streaming endpoints during the window
- No cold-start stalls during demos (they will run scheduled demos on week 2)
- Cannot accept dropped capacity mid-demo

Business context: this pilot is the gating item for a potential enterprise contract (Deal DH-4782). If pilot meets SLAs, Orion intends to move to Dedicated capacity in Q4. Product would like this prioritized and is asking for a temporary exception to the autoscale policy rather than full reserved commit.

Ask to ops/infra: can we offer a constrained, time-windowed safeguard reservation (Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 PST) for 3 weeks with conditional autoscale suppression? If yes, what tradeoffs and telemetry requirements do you need? If not, what mitigations can we propose (e.g., guaranteed warm cache + burst fallback + limited credits)?

I appreciate quick triage — customer expects a published plan by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benito Ruiz <benito@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request

Sergio —

Quick read on feasibility: we can do a time-windowed safeguard but there are several operational implications to call out before committing. Questions/concerns below so we can size impact and propose a safe path:

1) GPU type and exact slice: you specified A100-class single-GPU workers. Confirm model size and memory footprint (these determine whether they truly need A100 vs larger/quantized variant).

2) Hard reservation vs soft hold: you asked to disable autoscale for the window. That means we must guarantee those slots will not be reclaimed for other customers between 07:00–19:00. That reduces available pool for urgent ops events — we need an explicit carve duration and approval.

3) Canary & eviction triggers: we require an automatic eviction policy if a node shows repeated OOMs, kernel crashes, or SLO regressions. The exception cannot bypass safety eviction.

4) Telemetry & instrumentation: we need per-request trace IDs and a small query set for quality checks (product to supply). Also require a flag in the request to indicate pilot traffic for billing/trace.

5) Cost & credits: holding 6–8 slots 12h/day for 3 weeks is material. Ops will produce an uplift estimate. Finance should confirm whether we offer a pilot credit and how much.

Alternatives if we cannot fully reserve:
- Offer 6-slot reservation + 2-slot burst buffer (burst lanes) with guaranteed warm cache and prioritized routing for pilot traffic during demo windows.
- Provide cache-warming hooks (KV priming job) plus preloaded activations before demos.

If we go ahead, I will need inventory tagging (pilot:orion/DH-4782), the exact window in UTC, and a hard expiry date for the carve.

Attaching runbook excerpt and a checklist we will use if this is approved.

Laura
Capacity & Ops
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benito Ruiz <benito@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request

Agree with Laura — we should enable this pilot with strict guardrails. From product perspective:

Why now: this pilot unlocks a large inbound ARR motion (Orion has confirmed a 6–8 month procurement runway to Dedicated after a successful pilot). They will be requesting predictable latency for triage workflows integrated into their clinician UI — a clear revenue path.

Proposed compromise (to limit blast radius):
- Start with 6 slots guaranteed during pilot window. Increase to 8 only if telemetry in week 1 supports it.
- Autoscale suppression limited to core window (07:00–19:00 PST). Outside the window, normal autoscale behavior applies.
- Implement warm-cache priming (product team will provide sample prompt sets) and a demo day protection window where we temporarily bump priority routing (2 hours per demo).
- Pilot credit: product recommends 50% credit on reserved hours for the 3-week pilot to offset Ops cost and speed approval.

We need the following for me to escalate and sign off: expected RPS and peak token/sec from the traffic_forecast.csv, the exact model (or a Redwood catalog model id), and a go/no-go date for week 1.

Kimberly
Senior PM, Dedicated Capacity
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benito Ruiz <benito@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request

Thanks for the context. Technical stance: we can support a temporary exception with the following hard constraints and instrumentation requirements. I will own the infra changes and rollout with ops.

Constraints:
- Max initial reservation: 6 A100-class single-GPU slots (we can expand to 8 after week 1 review).
- Window enforcement: Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 PST; outside that the autoscaler can reclaim unallocated capacity.
- Safety eviction: automatic eviction still applies for node-level failures; exception only disables proactive downscaling due to low utilization.

Instrumentation required before enabling:
- Tag all pilot requests with header X-Redwood-Pilot: DH-4782 and include trace_id (per-request).
- Export per-slot CPU/GPU utilization and 95/99 latency metrics to the pilot dashboard.
- Implement a lightweight canary checker that runs five synthetic requests every 10 minutes and flips traffic to fallback if failure rate > 2% for 5 consecutive checks.

Operational guardrails:
- Hard expiry timestamp: reservation auto-reverts at 2027-07-22T07:00:00-07:00 unless extended by ops/product approval.
- Eviction trigger: repeated OOM/kernel panics will force immediate rollback of reservation.
- Inventory tag: pilot:orion/DH-4782 added to instances and to infra tickets.

I'll draft the infra change and the checklist (reservation-approval-checklist.pdf) and schedule a rollout window tonight (no customer traffic affected during rollout). We will also provide the uplift cost numbers for finance.

Dev
Staff Infra Engineer
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Benito Ruiz <benito@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orion Health pilot reserve: temporary safeguard & autoscale exception request

Thanks everyone — this is actionable and clean. Summary & next steps:

1) Scope: Approve 6-slot reservation, Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 PST, 3 weeks (2027-07-01 through 2027-07-22). Option to expand to 8 after week 1 review.
2) Instrumentation: Dev to deploy tracing and canary checks before reservation goes live. Tagging and inventory to be completed by ops.
3) Safety: Eviction and rollback triggers remain in place per Dev/Laura notes.
4) Billing: Product recommends 50% pilot credit; finance to confirm.
5) Customer comms: Sergio will send an updated pilot plan to Benito with the timeline, confirmed protections, and the DocuSign link.

Benito — I will send a single-sheet pilot runbook and the DocuSign link for the pilot agreement after infra confirms the rollout window. Expect the runbook + agreement by EOD today.

Sergio
